title: What Happens to Your leg tendons If You do 100 squats Every Day
description: One hundred squats a day. Your leg muscles will complain, but the real story is in the tendons that turn those squats into spring. Take the squat test, get your number, and follow four weeks of daily hundreds.

scenes.narration: Feet shoulder width. | Squat non-stop. | Hips below knees. | Stand tall every rep. | Stop when form dies. | That count is your NUMBER. | Write it down. | One hundred a day | is the habit on trial. | What does it do | to your LEG TENDONS? | Muscle gets the credit. | The cables do the bouncing. | Week one is a warning. | Week four is the answer. | At the end | I grade your number.

scenes.label: THE LINE BETWEEN SOFT AND SPRINGY
scenes.sub: under 25: untrained - over 80: a hundred is easy
scenes.narration: Here is the line. Fifty clean squats in a row is where soft legs become springy ones. Under twenty five, your leg tendons are simply untrained, and volume fixes that fast. Over eighty, a hundred a day is already maintenance for you. Today you measured the starting point. The daily hundred is about to turn your legs into springs, one set at a time.

Week one is a warning, and you should respect it. Day two, your thighs stage a protest and stairs become negotiations. That is muscle soreness, and it fades by day five. Underneath it, something quieter is happening. Your knees and ankles are learning the groove, and the tendons are registering a hundred daily knocks. By Sunday the same hundred feels shorter.

Week two, the hundred becomes a rhythm instead of an event. You split it into sets without thinking. Week three, the bottom of the squat changes character. You stop sinking into it and start bouncing out of it. That bounce is tendon, storing energy and handing it back for free. Week four, retest your max. Most skinny guys add twenty to forty reps in a month. Watch your walking in week four and you will see the receipt. Your stride gets a quiet bounce, the kind children have and adults lose. That bounce is not youth returning. It is two tendons handing energy back instead of absorbing it, thousands of times a day. You trained a hundred squats. Life multiplied them into every step you take.

Here is the hidden system. Two great cables run your legs. The patellar tendon drives the knee, and the Achilles drives the ankle. Every squat loads both, and they are not passive ropes. They are springs that store energy when they stretch and return it when you stand. Load them daily and they weave fresh collagen, growing stiffer and springier. Muscle pushes you up. Tendon decides how much of that push is free. One more thing the cycle count explains. Tendon soreness from volume behaves differently from muscle soreness. Muscles complain loudly and forgive quickly. Tendons complain quietly and remember. That is why the daily hundred works: the dose is spread thin enough that the tissue can answer every day. Spread is not a compromise. Spread is the mechanism.
Squat with me. Smooth reps, full depth, stand tall. This is a piece of the daily hundred. Go.

The protocol: one hundred squats a day, split any way you like. Four sets of twenty five is the classic. Full depth, knees tracking over toes, heels down. The mistake is one heroic set of a hundred on day one, which buys you three days of stairs terror. The other mistake is half depth. The tendon only trains through the range you actually use, so use all of it.

So, your number. Under twenty five: untrained cables, and volume is about to change your legs fast. Twenty five to fifty: the spring is building. Over fifty: you are wired, and the daily hundred will keep the bounce sharp. Retest on day thirty, same rules, honest depth. Put your number in the comments. Just the number.
Thirty days from now your legs will bounce instead of push. Subscribe, and we retest together. This is {channel}. Train the cable.
